card.name: Linking words before a qualifying clause
card.fires_on: Small linking words or punctuation right after a full subject in a medical statement, such as a comma, closing parenthesis, 'be' or 'are'. The next words add a qualifier, such as 'possibly leading to' or 'highest among'.

modes.label: Comma or bracket closing a clause
modes.description: A comma or closing parenthesis after a complete statement, before a trailing qualifier.
modes.example: cause a shift in potassium from the extracellular to intracellular space<<,>> possibly leading to hypokalemia.

modes.label: Verb after a subject
modes.description: The verb 'be' or 'are' after a subject, before a predicate adjective such as 'highest' or 'toxic'.
modes.example: Although the prevalence of the syndrome appears to<< be>> highest among the elderly, especially elderly women

card.plain: It fires at the small joining word that follows a finished claim, just before the sentence adds a qualifier or description.
